objects: For measures μ and ν on E, a coupling is exactly a measure γ on E×E whose first and second projection pushforwards are μ and ν. For κ:E×E→[0,∞], define C_κ(μ,ν)=inf{∫⁻ κ(z) dγ(z) : γ is such a coupling}. This is the infimum in the extended nonnegative reals; an empty feasible set has infimum ∞. The supplied definition imposes no additional condition on γ and makes no assertion that the infimum is attained. Write μ_t=(X(t,·))#P. This map function is determined by the explicitly supplied measurable proof hX(t), including hX(p.1) and hX(q.1) when product points are used. In this target κ(z) is c(z) coerced from the finite nonnegative reals into [0,∞].
domains: T is an arbitrary topological space with a first-countable topology. Ω is a measurable space and P is a probability measure on Ω. E is a compact topological space equipped with a measurable space, with the assumption that every open subset of the topological product E×E is measurable for its product measurable structure. No equality of the measurable structure with the Borel structure, Hausdorff condition, metrizability, or first-countability of E is stated. X:T→Ω→E and c:E×E→[0,∞) is a continuous map taking finite nonnegative-real values. A point s∈T is specified. No measurable structure on T and no topological structure on Ω is required.
quantifiers: Universally quantify T, Ω, E and all the listed structures, then P and X. Assume measurability of X(t,·) for every t and the one almost-sure path-continuity condition. Universally choose the continuous c, assume c(x,x)=0 for every x∈E, and choose any s∈T. For each such set of data the asserted neighborhood-filter limit holds.
assumptions: For every t∈T, X(t,·):Ω→E is measurable. For P-almost every ω, the entire map t↦X(t,ω) is continuous on T. The finite nonnegative cost c is continuous on E×E and satisfies c(x,x)=0 for all x∈E. The compactness, first-countability and product-open-set measurability assumptions are exactly those in the domains slot. No joint measurability of (t,ω)↦X(t,ω), symmetry or triangle inequality for c, or separation property c(x,y)=0⇒x=y is assumed.
conclusion: As t tends to s in T, C_c(μ_t,μ_s) tends to 0 in [0,∞], where c is coerced into the extended nonnegative reals in the nonnegative integral. Precisely, t↦C_c((X(t,·))#P,(X(s,·))#P sends the neighborhood filter of s to the neighborhood filter of 0 in the extended nonnegative reals.
scopes: This is a topological limit of deterministic extended-nonnegative transport-cost values for each specified s, not an almost-sure limit of random variables. The path-continuity assumption is one P-almost-everywhere statement asserting continuity on all of T. Slice measurability is required for every t and the diagonal cost identity for every state. There is no finite time horizon, no restriction to an ordered time set, and no uniform-in-s convergence conclusion. No metric or Wasserstein interpretation of this general cost is asserted.
constant_dependencies: No numerical bound, rate, modulus, or existential constant is part of the statement. The limit depends on the selected P, X, c, spaces and base point s; the theorem asserts the limit separately for every such choice.
